topic_tag: a freighter wreck off an island
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Divers who surveyed it in 2005 called the hull a true ______, and their photographs show why.

worlds.passage: In 1911 a steel freighter sank on a reef off a small island, where its hull still lies nearly whole. Divers who surveyed it in 2005 called the hull a true ______, and their photographs show why. Corals and sponges grow out along every beam and rail, while the sand around it, at the same depth, is bare. Its bow rises to twelve feet below the surface, and the only boats crossing there are island ferries drawing six. Its holds are still sealed, and its manifest lists them full of coal. The twenty-eight men aboard all appear in the island church's register at its next service.
worlds.explanation: Corals and sponges grow along every beam while the sand around the hull at the same depth is bare, so the growth exists because the hull gives it something to climb: a "trellis." A "tripwire" catches the unwary, but the bow lies twelve feet down and the only boats overhead draw six. A "strongbox" keeps something valuable secure, but the sealed holds keep only coal. A "tomb" holds the dead, but the twenty-eight men aboard match the twenty-eight sailors in the island church's register at its next service, so the crew survived.

tomb.quote: appear in the island church's register at its next service

tomb.surface_fit: A sunken ship is the stock image of a sailors' grave, and the passage counts the men aboard, so tomb is the reader's first thought.
tomb.inference: twenty-eight men aboard and all twenty-eight in the island church's register at its next service means the crew got ashore alive, so no one lies in the hull

strongbox.quote: its manifest lists them full of coal

strongbox.surface_fit: Holds still sealed after a century are the very picture of a strongbox keeping its cargo safe.
strongbox.inference: the holds are sealed, but what they keep is coal, a cargo not worth guarding or raising, so the hull is not keeping anything of value secure

tripwire.surface_fit: A bow rising to within twelve feet of the surface is exactly the kind of hidden hazard a tripwire is.
tripwire.inference: the bow lies twelve feet down and the only boats over it reach six feet down, so every one clears it and it catches nothing
